subject.title: fix(compaction): prevent repeated restarts after safety timeouts

question: Should a compaction safety timeout permit one explicitly marked partial result to mutate session state during the bounded reason-owned settlement window?
rationale: Tests and live proof can establish mechanics, but only the compaction owner can define whether timeout rejection is an absolute state boundary or whether bounded cooperative completion is an accepted product invariant.

options.title: Accept bounded settlement
options.body: Approve the typed ten-second settlement token after the shared-helper regression is fixed, preserving completed chunks while rejecting unmarked, external-abort, and late results.

options.title: Require pre-timeout checkpointing
options.body: Keep timeout as an absolute mutation boundary and redesign chunk progress so durable checkpoints are committed before the wrapper reports timeout.

options.title: Decline partial persistence
options.body: Retain terminal timeout behavior and limit the fix to clearer guidance or timeout-budget changes, accepting that completed chunks restart.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded settlement
recommendation.body: Approve the typed ten-second settlement token after the shared-helper regression is fixed, preserving completed chunks while rejecting unmarked, external-abort, and late results.
